rows.head: The Predators beat the Stars
rows.story: Mavrik Bourque scored his first goal for Nashville with just under a minute left in the first to open the scoring. Ross Colton added the empty-netter with less than two minutes left to make it 2-0. With the goalie pulled and 35 seconds left, Wyatt Johnston pulled the Stars within one, and Jack Drury ended any hope of a comeback with an empty-netter with 15 seconds left.
rows.calls: Zero of two preview calls held

rows.head: Marchand has three assists as the Panthers beat the Senators
rows.story: Aleksander Barkov was back in the lineup after missing 22 games. Eetu Luostarinen got the scoring started for the Panthers late in the first. It was a busy second period.
rows.calls: Zero of two preview calls held

chips: First goal for a new club
rows.head: Farabee has a goal and an assist as the Flames take down the Penguins
rows.story: Tommy Novak struck first for the Penguins late in the first. The Flames scored four times in the second. Joel Farabee made it 1-1 for Calgary just 38 seconds into the second, and Brennan Othmann put the Flames ahead 2-1 early in the period.
rows.calls: Zero of three preview calls held

rows.head: Connor has a goal and two assists as the Jets get past the Bruins
rows.story: Kyle Connor scored his 20th of the season just over a minute in to open the scoring for the Jets. Morgan Geekie made it 1-1 for Boston on the power play early in the first, and Tyrel Bauer and Tanner Jeannot squared off midway through the period. Josh Morrissey restored the Jets’ lead late in the period.
rows.calls: Zero of two preview calls held

rows.head: The Mammoth end the Wild’s 15-game point streak
rows.story: Lawson Crouse struck first for the Mammoth early in the first. There were five goals in the second period alone. Jack McBain and Michael McCarron opened the second period with a fight, and Logan Cooley made it 2-0 for the Mammoth on the power play early in the period.
rows.calls: Both preview calls held

rows.head: Gritsyuk wins it in a shootout
rows.story: Nico Hischier struck first for the Devils midway through the first. The Blue Jackets’ Denton Mateychuk left in the first period and didn’t return. The next day, he was ruled out with a concussion.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Brossoit slams the door on the Sharks
rows.story: An ugly night for the Sharks. Judd Caulfield and Alex Killorn scored 30 seconds apart midway through the first to put the Ducks up 2-0. Cutter Gauthier extended the lead to 3-0 on the power play just over a minute later, and Ian Moore made it 4-0 midway through the second.
rows.calls: All four preview calls held

rows.head: Eklund forces a shootout with just three seconds left, and the Islanders win it
rows.story: Jean-Gabriel Pageau got the scoring started for the Islanders early in the second, but Dylan Holloway tied it 1-1 for St. Louis late in the period. Mason McTavish put the Blues ahead 2-1 with six minutes left.
rows.calls: Both preview calls held

rows.head: Kantserov has two goals as the Blackhawks hold off the Kraken
rows.story: Spencer Knight stopped Mackie Samoskevich on a penalty shot just over a minute in. The Blackhawks went more than 19 minutes without a shot on goal, from early in the second to early in the third. Most teams don’t go that long without a shot even once a season.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: The Capitals roll past the Flyers
rows.story: Travis Konecny got the scoring started for the Flyers just 17 seconds into the game, but Ryan Leonard tied it up for Washington a little over three minutes later. Cole Hutson gave the Capitals the lead on the power play midway through the second. Boone Jenner pushed the lead to 3-1 late in the period.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Blackwood shuts out the Canadiens
rows.story: An ugly night for the Canadiens. Logan O'Connor got the scoring started for the Avalanche midway through the first, and Artturi Lehkonen made it 2-0 just 30 seconds into the second. The Canadiens’ Kaiden Guhle left in the second period and didn’t return.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Slavin’s third-period goal lifts the Hurricanes past the Lightning
rows.story: Anthony Cirelli opened the scoring for the Lightning on the power play just 55 seconds into the second, but they didn’t score again. The Lightning’s Pontus Holmberg left in the second period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was ruled out for four weeks with a lower-body injury.
rows.calls: The preview call missed

rows.head: The Red Wings cruise past the Canucks
rows.story: Emmitt Finnie scored early in the first and again less than three minutes later to put the Red Wings up 2-0. Lucas Raymond made it 3-0 on the power play with just under a minute left in the period. J.T. Compher stretched the lead to 4-0 early in the second, but Paul Cotter got the Canucks on the board early in the third.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: The Sabres pile it on the Rangers
rows.story: Rasmus Dahlin got the scoring started for the Sabres just 17 seconds into the game. Josh Norris and Zach Benson scored 33 seconds apart early in the second to extend the lead to 3-0. Vladislav Gavrikov got the Rangers on the board with 46 seconds left in the period.
rows.calls: Zero of three preview calls held

rows.head: Keller sparks a Mammoth comeback
rows.story: The first period was a wild one. Filip Forsberg opened the scoring for the Predators just 52 seconds into the game, and Roman Josi extended the lead to 2-0 shorthanded late in the period. Clayton Keller and Mikhail Sergachev scored less than two minutes apart later in the period to tie it 2-2.
rows.calls: All three preview calls held

rows.head: Hughes forces a shootout with a minute left, and the Avalanche win it
rows.story: What a comeback. Joel Eriksson Ek and Blake Coleman scored less than five minutes apart in the first to put the Wild up 2-0. Eriksson Ek scored again with 44 seconds left in the second to make it 3-0.
rows.calls: Both preview calls held

rows.head: Gaudette has a goal and an assist as the Sharks take down the Golden Knights
rows.story: Michael Misa got the scoring started for the Sharks late in the second. It was a busy third period. Adam Gaudette stretched the lead to 2-0 early in the period, with Dmitry Orlov picking up his 300th NHL assist on the goal.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Mangiapane has two goals as the Blackhawks edge the Rangers
rows.story: Andrew Mangiapane struck first for the Blackhawks on the power play early in the first, and Matt Rempe and Dillon Boucher dropped the gloves midway through the period. Mika Zibanejad made it 1-1 for the Rangers on the power play late in the period, with J.T. Miller picking up his 500th NHL assist on the goal. Mangiapane scored again on the power play with just under a minute left in the period to put the Hawks ahead for good.
rows.calls: Both preview calls held

rows.head: Solberg scores his first two NHL goals, but the Ducks lose
rows.story: Stian Solberg, in his fifth NHL game, scored his first NHL goal, set up by Mikael Granlund, midway through the first to open the scoring for the Ducks. He scored his second NHL goal a little over a minute later to make it 2-0. It was a busy second period.
rows.calls: One of three preview calls held

rows.head: Four points for Jack Hughes as the Devils beat the Flames
rows.story: Joel Hanley got the scoring started for the Flames late in the first. The second period was a wild one. Luke Hughes and Timo Meier scored just 12 seconds apart early in the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead.
rows.calls: Both preview calls held

rows.head: Holloway has two goals and an assist as the Blues hold off the Stars
rows.story: Philip Broberg opened the scoring for the Blues just 26 seconds into the game, and Robert Thomas stretched the lead to 2-0 midway through the first. Roope Hintz and Jason Robertson scored power-play goals just over a minute apart midway through the second to tie it 2-2. It was a busy third period.
rows.calls: The preview call missed

rows.head: Kakko has two goals as the Kraken hold off the Oilers
rows.story: Jordan Eberle struck first for the Kraken midway through the first, but Connor McDavid tied it 1-1 for Edmonton on the power play early in the second. Leon Draisaitl gave the Oilers the lead midway through the period, and that was all they would get. Joey Daccord took over from Philipp Grubauer in net for Seattle to start the third, after two goals against.
rows.calls: Zero of two preview calls held

rows.head: Bennett wins it with 24 seconds left
rows.story: Cole Hutson got the scoring started for the Capitals on the power play midway through the first. Aaron Ekblad tied it 1-1 for Florida on the power play early in the second. Hutson scored again with just under seven minutes left to put the Capitals back ahead 2-1, but Eetu Luostarinen tied it 2-2 for Florida with a little over four minutes left.
rows.calls: Zero of two preview calls held

rows.head: Gibson slams the door on the Blue Jackets
rows.story: J.T. Compher opened the scoring for the Red Wings midway through the first, and Alex DeBrincat made it 2-0 early in the third. Detroit had a goal taken off for offside with just seven seconds left, but it didn’t cost them in the end.
rows.calls: The preview call held

rows.head: Rielly scores twice as the Maple Leafs beat the Bruins
rows.story: Morgan Rielly, who scores in about 1 game in 11, scored twice. Casey Mittelstadt opened the scoring for the Bruins on the power play early in the first, but they didn’t score again. The Bruins’ David Pastrňák left in the first period and didn’t return.
rows.calls: Zero of two preview calls held

rows.head: The Senators run away from the Lightning
rows.story: Ridly Greig struck first for the Senators early in the first, and Tim Stützle stretched the lead to 2-0 shorthanded midway through the period. Michael Amadio made it 3-0 early in the second. Gage Goncalves and Nick Cousins squared off midway through the period.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Konecny has a goal and an assist as the Flyers beat the Canucks
rows.story: Tyson Foerster struck first for the Flyers on the power play early in the first. The Canucks’ Filip Chytil left early in the second period and didn’t return. Noah Cates made it 2-0 for the Flyers early in the period, and Porter Martone stretched the lead to 3-0 on the power play midway through the period.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

chips: First goal for a new club
rows.head: Connor has two goals and an assist as the Jets beat the Islanders
rows.story: Kyle Connor got the scoring started for the Jets late in the first. Gabriel Vilardi extended the lead to 2-0 early in the second, and that one stood up as the winner. Connor scored again on the power play late in the period to make it 3-0.
rows.calls: The preview call held

rows.head: Malkin has a goal and an assist as the Penguins take down the Sabres
rows.story: It was a busy first period. Jiří Kulich opened the scoring for the Sabres just 31 seconds into the game, his fourth straight game with a goal. Ben Kindel made it 1-1 for Pittsburgh early in the first, and Rasmus Dahlin restored the Sabres’ lead on the power play less than two minutes later.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Draisaitl’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The teams have split two meetings this season. The Kraken are 12-10-1, while the Oilers are winless in five (0-4-1). This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Oilers first (third in the NHL) and the Kraken fourth (tied for 22nd).

rows.head: Two of the best
rows.story: The Hurricanes have won three straight, and the Senators (17-7-3) beat Tampa Bay 6-2 last night. Two of the league’s best teams meet. Going in, the Senators are first in the Atlantic (fourth in the NHL) and the Canes first in the Metropolitan (second).

rows.head: McMichael meets his old team
rows.story: The Capitals (11-12-0) lost 3-2 to Florida last night, while the Blues (14-9-3) beat Dallas 5-3 the same night. Going in, the Caps are sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Blues sixth in the Central (tied for 14th). The Capitals have played better than their record (.478) says: their chances are worth about .578, and losses in one-goal games have held them back.

rows.head: Johnston’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The Stars (15-8-2) lost 5-3 to St. Louis last night, while the Mammoth have won two in a row. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Mammoth seventh (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Stars fourth (tied for ninth).

rows.head: Panarin’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The Kings won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-3 in Anaheim last night. The Kings have won two in a row, while the Ducks are 12-14-1. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Ducks fifth (tied for 22nd in the NHL) and the Kings seventh (29th).

rows.head: Something has to give
rows.story: The Panthers have won three straight, while the Lightning are on a three-game losing streak. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Lightning third (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Panthers second (tied for seventh). This season, the Panthers have outscored teams 84-76, even though they’ve been outscored 50-44 at 5-on-5.

rows.head: The Islanders’ defense joins the attack, the Flyers’ stays home
rows.story: The Islanders (12-8-5) lost 3-1 to Winnipeg last night, while the Flyers (10-12-6) beat Vancouver 5-2 the same night. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Islanders third (17th in the NHL) and the Flyers fifth (tied for 19th). The Islanders’ record (.580) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.492), largely thanks to their goaltending.

rows.head: Crosby’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The Penguins (8-15-2) beat Buffalo 6-3 last night, and the Maple Leafs have won two in a row. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. Going in, the Maple Leafs are last in the Atlantic (tied for 25th in the NHL) and the Pens last in the Metropolitan (31st).

rows.head: Where the Predators have the edge: the penalty kill
rows.story: The Red Wings have won two in a row, while the Predators (13-6-6) lost 6-5 in a shootout to Utah last night. Going in, the Predators are third in the Central (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Red Wings seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 25th). The Predators’ record (.640) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.526), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

rows.head: A good test for both
rows.story: The Golden Knights (15-7-5) lost 4-1 to San Jose last night, and the Canadiens are on a three-game losing streak. Two good teams meet. Going in, the Habs are fourth in the Atlantic (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Golden Knights second in the Pacific (sixth).

rows.head: The Devils’ power play has a target
rows.story: The Jets won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-2 in Winnipeg on Nov 10. Both teams come in on a three-game winning streak. Going in, the Jets are fifth in the Central (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Devils second in the Metropolitan (fifth).

rows.head: A long night for Alex Nedeljkovic
rows.story: The Avalanche have won three straight, and the Sharks (12-14-2) beat Vegas 4-1 last night. Going in, the Sharks are third in the Pacific (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Avalanche second in the Central (tied for seventh). The Sharks are one of the league’s most physical teams (3rd), ice the puck a lot (32nd) and have a leaky penalty kill (31st).

rows.head: Picky vs. trigger-happy
rows.story: The Rangers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Calgary on Nov 11. The Rangers are on a three-game losing streak, and the Flames (11-14-2) lost 5-3 to New Jersey last night. Going in, the Flames are sixth in the Pacific (24th in the NHL) and the Rangers fourth in the Metropolitan (18th).

rows.head: The Bruins are likely to drive the play
rows.story: The Bruins (15-9-1) lost 3-1 to Toronto on Friday, and the Canucks are on a three-game losing streak. Going in, the Canucks are last in the NHL and the Bruins fifth in the Atlantic (tied for 14th in the NHL). The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.232) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .343, and their goaltending has held them back.

rows.note: Who drives the play: the Wild
rows.head: The Blackhawks are rolling
rows.story: The Blackhawks have won four straight, while the Wild (18-4-6) lost 4-3 in a shootout to Colorado on Friday. Going in, the Wild are first in the NHL and the Blackhawks last in the Central (tied for 27th in the NHL). The Wild’s record (.750) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.633), largely thanks to their goaltending.

rows.head: Somebody has to win
rows.story: The Blue Jackets won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in a shootout in Columbus on Oct 9. The Penguins (8-15-2) beat Buffalo 6-3 on Friday, while the Blue Jackets are winless in three (0-2-1). Both teams are near the bottom of the standings.

rows.head: Who blinks first?
rows.story: The Canadiens won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-4 in overtime in Montréal on Nov 5. The Mammoth have won two in a row, while the Canadiens are on a three-game losing streak. Going in, the Habs are fourth in the Atlantic (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Mammoth seventh in the Central (tied for 14th).

rows.head: Benoit returns to Toronto
rows.story: The Maple Leafs have won two in a row, and the Flyers (10-12-6) beat Vancouver 5-2 on Friday. Going in, the Flyers are fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Leafs last in the Atlantic (tied for 25th). The Flyers’ record (.464) is about what their chances are worth.

rows.head: Unstoppable force vs. immovable object
rows.story: The Hurricanes already played in New York once this season and left with a 5-2 win on Nov 22. The Rangers are on a three-game losing streak, while the Hurricanes have won three straight. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Canes first (second in the NHL) and the Rangers fourth (18th).

rows.head: The Blackhawks are on a heater
rows.story: The teams have split two meetings this season. The Jets have won three straight, and the Blackhawks have won four straight. The Blackhawks played last night, and the Jets are rested.

rows.head: Tilted ice, toward the Predators’ net
rows.story: The Senators won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in a shootout in Ottawa on Oct 10. The Senators (17-7-3) beat Tampa Bay 6-2 on Friday, while the Predators (13-6-6) lost 6-5 in a shootout to Utah the same night. Going in, the Sens are first in the Atlantic (fourth in the NHL) and the Predators third in the Central (tied for ninth).

standout.head: Kyle Connor put 9 shots on goal
standout.sub: Only 12 other games this season have matched it, moving him from 3rd to 1st.
